photos.caption: Rural homestead, weathered and simple.
photos.description: Two buildings stand side-by-side on stilts, with a corrugated iron roof and a raised veranda. The foreground is filled with tall, dry grasses, and a weathered water tank is visible on the left.

photos.caption: A woman sewing at home.

photos.caption: A quiet family remembrance moment.

remembrance.title: For Rosa Delgado, who always kept the kettle on
remembrance.text:
We’ve set out a little of everything she loved. The pan de muerto is for her, of course, and a pot of café de olla to always be ready. We remember her saying, “Come in, there’s coffee,” and we want to offer that warmth to her now. The orange marigolds, bright and cheerful, just like she was.

In the photo at the sewing machine, you can see her, focused and happy, letting us choose the buttons from her biscuit tin. She spent so many Saturday afternoons listening to boleros on the radio, humming along while she cleaned. It’s a quiet comfort to remember that.

We’ve put out a tin of buttons, just like she always did, and we hope she hears us, enjoying the music and the simple pleasures she cherished.

prompt:
Write a short remembrance for an ofrenda, the altar families build for Día de los Muertos to welcome back the people they love.
Language: English. Length: 110 to 170 words, in 2 or 3 short paragraphs. Warm, simple and specific; not flowery, not sad for the sake of it.
Write about them in the third person, the way a family member would read it aloud.

STRICT RULE: use ONLY the facts below. Do not add any name, place, date, year, age, job, food, song, or event that is not written below.
If a detail isn't given, leave it out. It is better to be short than to invent.
Build it mainly from the family's memories: what they did, what they said, the habits people still talk about. Use most of them.
The photo notes were written by a computer: mention a photo at most once, briefly, as a photo ("in the photo at the sewing machine"). Never treat a photo's place or people as facts about their life.
End by naming a few of their favourite things as the offerings placed on the ofrenda for them.
Answer format: the title on the first line (2 to 6 words, using their name, e.g. "For [name], who always kept the kettle on"),
then a blank line, then the remembrance. Plain text only: no markdown, no headings, no notes before or after.

FACTS (written by their family):
Name: Rosa Delgado
Years: 1931 – 2019
Who they were to the writer: my grandmother
Favourite things, placed on the ofrenda: pan de muerto; café de olla; boleros on the radio; a tin of buttons; orange marigolds
Memories:
"""
She ran a small bakery with my grandfather and got up at four every morning to light the ovens.
She always said "Come in, there's coffee" before you were even through the door.
She sewed all of our Halloween costumes on her old sewing machine, and let us pick the buttons from her biscuit tin.
On Saturday afternoons she listened to boleros on the radio and hummed along while she cleaned.
"""
